subject: Texas AI Docket, Carousel No. 3, August 19th, 2026, The deadline ERCOT set itself, and what happened to it
body:
The deadline ERCOT set itself, and what happened to it

Carousel No. 3, August 19th, 2026

Did NOT meet the bar: 6.82 against 7.0. Read before posting.

This run did not merge, so the images below come from the run branch claude/daily-2026-08-19 rather than from main. They stop resolving if that branch is deleted.

claimsPASS, 21 verified, 7 rejected
copy syncPASS, 8 slides match what the browser laid out
coherencePASS, reading load max 42 against a 65 ceiling, counter spine correct
aggregatesPASS, every declaration on the frame that ships it
sources blockPASS, all 16 printed claim ids resolve across 6 documents
dossiersPASS, 8 slides planned, every band answered
bespokePASS at 0.2717 against a 0.55 fail line
captionPASS, 160 words, 3 of 3 hashtags
machine QAWARN, 0 fails, 4 frame balance warns
assemblyPASS, 8 slides, vector PDF
scoreHOLD at 6.82 against a 7.0 threshold

What degraded

  • THE DECK DOES NOT SHIP. It scored 6.82 against a 7.0 threshold on its fourth pass.
    The score stopped climbing. 6.51, then 6.87, then 6.932, then 6.82. Artwork, story and voice all lost ground to one cause the scorer named plainly: the deck is procedurally impeccable and has no place and no person in it. That is a story selection finding rather than a frame to redraw, so a fifth pass would be polishing away from the actual cause. The run branch carries the evidence and nothing merged to main.
  • The deck ships 8 slides rather than 9
    The scorer named slide 4 the most cuttable frame twice. Its headline promised whose water and whose power and the frame delivered only water. Cutting it freed the close, which had no way for a reader to act.
  • No cartography anywhere, and no county or town named
    The record carries no geography for this statewide item, so a locator map would be decoration. All three treatment directors reached that independently. It is the honest call and the fourth pass showed it is also what holds the deck under the line.
  • The strongest discovery of the day was held rather than admitted
    The Atlas Energy and Kodiak driverless proppant fleet in the Permian has dated primary corporate sources and a schedule from 28 trucks to 100. No source names its Texas county, and the repo's gazetteer carries counties rather than cities, so Kermit cannot be resolved to Winkler from data this project holds. A statewide flag would be a claim about scope nobody checked.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it The deadline ERCOT set itself, and what happened to it, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

4 days of notice. 16 days since the letter.

Governor Abbott's letter reached ERCOT on August 3rd. ERCOT was to tell providers how each large load in Batch Zero was classified by August 7th. It told the market that date would not hold. ERCOT committed to seek a good cause exception from the Public Utility Commission ahead of the August 20th open meeting. That meeting is 1 day out.

The press release says the audit must be complete "before any data center project moves forward". The signed letter says "before any additional data centers are approved to move forward". Same office, same day.

On August 18th the Governor's office said the sector's membership body will comply with his standards.

The deck sets both wordings in facing columns, gives a blank field to the one project no source names, and closes on every date and docket still open to you.

Which wording would a Texas county plan around?

#ERCOT #PUCT #BatchZero

2. The first comment

Day counts computed in compute.py from the source dates above.

The machine changed itself

  • the post takes its hashtags back, and a gate holds them there
    config/brand.yaml has always required three. knowledge/carousel/CAPTION_CRAFT.md listed hashtags under banned furniture as engagement bait, so run 2 shipped a post with none while every gate stayed green. A rule stated in config, a surface that ignored it, and nothing in between.
  • a new gate, coherence_check: the deck reads as one object
    the 2026-08-16 deck shipped eight slides with no progress counter anywhere and the 2026-08-18 deck shipped nine with one on every slide. Both were green on every gate that existed, because brand.yaml fixes the counter and nothing connected a check to it.
  • a count means the thing its own noun names
    a slide read 'three sources' over two distinct documents and aggregate_check re-derived it against len(from_claims), which is three claim ids. The gate confirmed a published miscount.
  • the render report window was 80 characters, so a gate could not see past it
    aggregate_check scans that report. Slide 1 was stored truncated mid sentence, so 'That date passed 12 days ago' was invisible to the one gate whose job is catching an invented number. Widened to 320, and the gate immediately demanded a declaration it had passed over in silence on every previous run.
  • the render report declares its own text window
    widening that constant made copy_sync_check compare every ARCHIVED report against today's value, so the 2026-08-16 deck went red on a deck that had not changed. The ruler had. A constant in the consumer is the wrong place for a fact about how an artifact was produced.
  • a new gate, sources_block: every claim id the deck prints must resolve
    first_comment.txt is the only place a reader can turn a printed id back into a document. This deck printed sixteen and the block listed seven. Nine resolved to nothing, including all three claims the run added and four of the five on the closing frame. claims_check, copy_sync_check and aggregate_check all passed, because none of them looks at a text file of prose.
  • bespoke_check was measuring the standing masthead rather than the drawings
    the coherence upgrade above put the wordmark, star, kicker, site line and counter on every frame, which is the point of them. This gate scored that consistency as sameness. On the closest pair it shared 50 tokens and exactly one was a drawing call, and the deck failed at 0.5508 against a 0.55 line on furniture alone. Same fault as the FURNITURE set one layer up, which is a vocabulary of CSS and JS keywords and could never catch markup introduced afterwards.

Each reverts on its own commit.

Notes

THE RECORD. The worklist cleared in full. The selector named 46 items, all 46 were re-verified against one primary source each, and 50 items carry a dated movement line for today. Movement coverage went from 19 of 61 to 61 of 61, so "How this decision moved" no longer renders empty on two thirds of the record. The backlog holds at 3, the three items exempt by name. Real movement found on four items. The Governor's August 3rd directive has already cost a deadline. ERCOT said it would not tell service providers how any large load is classified in the Batch Zero study by August 7th, and that it would ask the commission for a good cause exception ahead of the August 20th open meeting. The Governor's office said on August 18th that the Data Center Coalition will comply and that one data center that could not comply ended operations before construction began. THE RUN'S WORST MOMENT. The commission's filing search and calendar feed returned HTTP 503 to every fetch across the whole run, and four items were written up as unconfirmed and committed that way. Reading this project's own sources field log to write today's entry is what caught it, because that file already carries the rule that a tool level failure is not a property of the source. Retested with a browser user agent. All four answered 200, and Project 58482 had taken a comment on August 18th that this run was about to miss entirely. Three status codes have now been recorded against those hosts by three clients on three days, 402 and 503 and 200, and the host was serving on all three. THE DECK HELD, FOUR TIMES. 6.51, then 6.87, then 6.932, then 6.82. Every finding from every pass was acted on and the acted-on items are the deck's best work now. The fourth pass is where it stopped being worth another round. Three of the four criteria that lost ground lost it to the same thing. A statewide procedural story left the deck with no county, no town and no person in it. No redraw fixes that. Nothing merged to main and the run branch carries all of it.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck did NOT merge, so nothing here is on main and there is nothing to post. The links resolve against the run branch for as long as it exists.
